title: Credibility Assessment of CFD Models for Aerosol Deposition in Respiratory Drug Delivery Under NASA-STD-7009A

models.name: Patient-Specific Airway LES with Lagrangian Particles (PS-LES-LPT)
models.what_it_computes: Transient inhalation airflow in reconstructed upper airways using large-eddy simulation, and polydisperse particle trajectories via Lagrangian tracking to compute surface-resolved and regional deposition fractions from mouth through segmental bronchi.

models.name: Device-Resolved Spray RANS with Population Balance and 1D Lung Coupling (DRS-PBM-1D)
models.what_it_computes: Internal nozzle flow, primary atomization, and droplet size–velocity distributions using RANS coupled to a population balance model; near-field oropharyngeal deposition and regional delivery to conducting airways via a coupled 1D airway network.

mechanisms.name: Inertial impaction during high-momentum inhalation and actuation overlap
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Determines oropharyngeal losses and achievable lung dose for spray-based delivery, influencing efficacy and local exposure in the mouth–throat.

mechanisms.name: Gravitational sedimentation and diffusion during post-inhalation breath-hold
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Controls fine-particle delivery to distal conducting airways, relevant to targeting small-airway disease and minimizing proximal deposition.

clear_factors: Relevance of the quantities of interest

deviation.detail: All factor scores are reported on a proprietary 0–7 integer scale with anchors at 0 (insufficient), 3 (adequate), and 7 (strong), assigned separately for each model–mechanism pair.
